title: Context limits and evidence selection
goals: Account for fixed text, evidence and reserved output under a toy budget
Select complete evidence for a stated question
Handle insufficient or conflicting evidence explicitly

prerequisite.prompt: Does lower next-token loss guarantee supported factual answers?
prerequisite.answer: No. Evaluate retrieval and claim support directly using sources and task-specific criteria.

vocabulary: The permitted input and output allocation under a stated model or classroom contract
Choosing source material relevant to the requested claim
Capacity deliberately kept available for the response
Removing part of a sequence to meet a limit

blocks.text: For this lesson only, a fictional system allows 100 total token units for input plus reserved output. Its fixed instructions use 20 units, question 10 and output reserve 20. That leaves 50 units for evidence. These are supplied counts, not word counts or a claim about any deployed model. Other systems can use different input/output accounting, so read their exact contract.

The question is: “Which room is approved for the robotics meeting, and what is its capacity?” Evidence A, a current approval notice, costs 30 units and names room B. Evidence B, the current room register, costs 20 and gives room B capacity 12. Evidence C, an old approval notice, costs 25 and names room A.

A+B costs 50 and fits exactly. Together they support both requested claims. A+C costs 55 and exceeds the evidence budget, while C+B fits at 45 but supplies an outdated room decision. A cheap set is not necessarily an adequate set. Preserve document IDs, versions and dates alongside content.

blocks.title: Keep the evidence roles separate
rows: Do not invent the missing fact
blocks.caption: Arithmetic fit and evidential adequacy are separate checks.

blocks.text: A source may contain an exception after a general statement. Cutting off the last paragraph can reverse its practical meaning. Selection should preserve the passages needed to interpret the requested fact, including scope, version and exceptions. If complete relevant evidence cannot fit, retrieve a smaller authoritative passage or request clarification rather than silently remove a qualifying condition.

Including a document in context does not prove the generated answer uses it correctly. After generation, check each claim against its source. A source’s instruction-like content also does not acquire authority just because it fits in the evidence budget.

Supported total 80, fixed instructions 15, question 10 and reserved output 15 leave 40 units. Two complete relevant passages cost 18 and 22, fitting exactly. A third irrelevant passage costs 8; adding it would exceed the stated total. A short summary can reduce size but must retain claim-supporting qualifiers and be checked against the original.

blocks.label: Guided: calculate the available evidence units and explain why exact fit does not prove answer correctness.

lesson.title: State the fallback before using the system

blocks.text: If room approval is missing, do not infer it from capacity. If sources conflict without a documented current version, report the conflict or ask the responsible person. Keep the requested claim, budget calculation, selected source IDs and unresolved facts in the record. This classroom accounting develops the reasoning without needing a live model.

blocks.label: Exit: A is unavailable and B gives only room capacity. Write a response that reports the supported fact without claiming the meeting is approved there.

workbook.title: Compute available evidence
workbook.prompt: Under total 100, instructions 20, question 10 and output reserve 20, calculate evidence capacity.

workbook.title: Choose complete support
workbook.prompt: Compare A+B,A+C,C+B for fit and support of current approval and capacity.
workbook.answer: Teacher explanation: A+B costs 50 and supports both. A+C costs 55 and fails budget; C+B costs 45 but uses old approval and fails current-approval support.

workbook.title: Preserve a qualifier
workbook.prompt: A passage says room B normally holds 12, except during maintenance when the approved limit is 8. Why is retaining only the first clause inadequate?
workbook.answer: Teacher explanation: The exception changes the applicable capacity during maintenance. Preserve conditions and determine whether maintenance applies; do not report 12 unconditionally.

workbook.title: Budget new evidence independently
workbook.prompt: Total 120, instructions 25, question 15, output reserve 30. Source D is current approval, cost 28; E is current capacity, cost 22; F is old approval, cost 18. Compute capacity, compare D+E and E+F, and state an honest fallback if D is missing.
workbook.answer: Teacher explanation: Evidence capacity 50. D+E costs 50 and supplies both current claims. E+F costs 40 but old approval is insufficient. Without D, report the supported capacity and ask for current approval rather than infer it.

workbook.title: Audit inclusion
workbook.prompt: A team says every claim is verified because all chosen documents fit in context. What further check is needed?
workbook.answer: Teacher explanation: Check each generated claim against the actual source passage/version and preserve qualifiers. Budget fit and inclusion do not establish faithful use or current correctness.

teacher.background: Use two 45-minute sessions. All model outputs and probability tables are constructed classroom examples. No hosted AI service, external API or student account is needed. Distinguish a model objective from factual support and system permissions. Collect independent work before discussing its solutions.
materials: Printed lesson and workbook; paper and pencil
Prepare the independent task and fresh retry without displaying solutions
sessions: Retrieve the prerequisite and distinguish a numerical claim from its interpretation.
Read section 1 and complete W1; ask for a reason alongside each answer.
Trace the worked case in section 2 and complete W2.
Discuss the diagram and complete W3 in pairs; record support.
Complete the guided response before sharing the answer.
Read the remaining sections and trace another constructed case.
Collect W4 independently, requiring calculations and a bounded conclusion.
Discuss W5 and the exit response. Provide feedback and a fresh retry.
teacher.guidedAnswer: Guided: 80-15-10-15 = 40; 18+22 fits. Claim support must still be checked. Exit: the register lists room B capacity 12, but current meeting approval is unavailable; request that approval before naming it as approved.
misconceptions: The lesson uses supplied counts; actual counts depend on tokenizer and protocol.
The smallest set is the best evidence
A set can fit while lacking current support for the requested claims.
Generation may misread or ignore evidence; verify claims after generation.
teacher.assessment: W4 requires 50, exact D+E fit, E+F inadequacy and an explicit missing-approval fallback. Fresh retry: total 90,instructions 20,question 10,reserve 20 gives 40; current approval costs 24 and capacity 16, exactly fit. A cost-12 old approval does not replace current support.
teacher.support: Provide labelled intermediate columns and allow a calculator. Ask students to state the meaning and denominator of a value before interpreting it. Extension: implement the classroom calculation locally and test boundary cases without using personal data.
teacher.next: Week 11 writes response specifications with explicit evidence requirements, output fields and fallback behaviour.
